title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to a list of open problems or remarks (items b–g) on the divided-power de Rham complex C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_*, k) of a simplicial set X_*. That complex is an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms. It is built from divided-power polynomial forms on the standard simplices, bigraded so that each bidegree is finite free; the previous page has a k{T}. Item (e) recalls an elementary fact about ordinary cochains and proposes the analogue for the pd de Rham complex.

(1) Ordinary case. The chain complex C_·(X_*, Z) is the primitive object. It gives C_·(X_*, k) = C_·(X_*, Z) ⊗_Z k, and every cochain complex C^·(X_*, k') = Hom^·_Z(C_·(X_*, Z), k'), for any k-algebra k'.

(2) Proposal. Construct a 'chain' version C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, k). This is a differential bigraded co-bialgebra (cobigèbre) with a k-coaugmentation and a 'divided' comultiplication, i.e. dual to the divided-power multiplication. It should satisfy, compatibly with all structures:
- C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_*, k') ≅ Hom_k(C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, k), k'),
- base change C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, k') ≅ C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, k) ⊗_k k'.

In modern terms: take, for each simplex Δ^n, the bidegree-wise linear dual of the pd form algebra Ω_pd(Δ^n). This is a cosimplicial-dual, i.e. simplicial, dg coalgebra. Then set C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*) = X_* ⊗_Δ (that object), a coend / left Kan extension along the Yoneda embedding. By construction it commutes with all colimits in X_*. The cochain functor, being Hom out of it, sends colimits to limits.

(3) Conclusion. The finest object is C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, Z), not its dual C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_*, Z). Grothendieck says this coalgebra should be used to attack (b) multiplicative structure, (c) reconstructing Steenrod/Whitney cohomology operations and (d) Sullivan-type minimal models, homotopy type and Künneth, without finiteness conditions on X_*. The final remark contrasts the two functors: the cochain version turns arbitrary colimits into limits, while the chain version commutes with arbitrary colimits, not merely filtered ones.

The purpose is to find an integral, colimit-preserving, coalgebraic chain-level model for the homotopy type of simplicial sets, of which the pd-de Rham cochain algebra is the dual.
errors: No real error. The duality Hom_k(C^{DRpd}_{··}, k') ≅ C^{··}_{DRpd}(·, k') can only hold because each bidegree of Ω_pd(Δ^n) is finite free (via the weight / second grading). Taking the plain dual of the total, infinite-rank complex would give products instead of direct sums. The page does not state this hypothesis explicitly.
The insertion correcting 'k'-module' to 'k-alg.' is right: the cochain identification is meant to be multiplicative. For the purely linear statement a module would suffice.

'Co-bigèbre' (bialgebra) is asserted without saying which second multiplicative structure is meant. It is presumably the dual of the cup-type product together with the pd structure, or the structure coming from the k{T} variable. This is left vague.

ideas.what: Cochains with arbitrary coefficients are Hom out of integral chains, and chains with coefficients are a base change of integral chains; integral chains are the 'primitive' object.
ideas.modern_name: Universal coefficients / chains as primary object

ideas.what: A predual, chain-level divided-power de Rham object: a dg co-bialgebra with divided comultiplication, defined integrally, whose k'-linear dual is the pd de Rham cochain algebra and which satisfies base change.
ideas.modern_name: Coend / left Kan extension of the dual of simplicial pd polynomial forms; integral dg coalgebra model (cf. Quillen's dg coalgebra models; Goerss's simplicial coalgebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rationally: Quillen 1969 (dg coalgebras), Sullivan 1977 (forms). Integral divided-power form models: Cenkl–Porter, Karoubi (later, partially). Coalgebraic p-adic models without finiteness: Goerss 1995.
ideas.where_published: Only in these 1976 IHÉS lecture notes (cote 136)

ideas.what: Preferring the colimit-preserving coalgebra over the cochain algebra in order to remove finiteness hypotheses from homotopy-type reconstruction (minimal models, Steenrod operations, Künneth).
ideas.modern_name: Coalgebraic vs. algebraic models: cochain models need finite type (Sullivan, Mandell), coalgebra models do not (Goerss 1995)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goerss (Simplicial chains over a field and p-local homotopy theory, 1995); Mandell 2001/2006 for the finite-type cochain side

ideas.what: The chain-level functor commutes with all colimits, while the cochain functor transforms colimits into limits.
ideas.modern_name: Colimit-preservation of left Kan extensions / duality

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies, in 1976, the chain-level divided-power coalgebra (rather than the cochain algebra) as the correct integral model for attacking homotopy type and cohomology operations without finiteness conditions. This anticipates the later dichotomy between cochain-algebra models, which require finite type (Sullivan rationally, Mandell's E∞ theorem p-adically and integrally), and coalgebra models, which do not (Goerss 1995 p-adically). His version is integral and divided-power, which does not seem to have been developed.
missed.quote: L'objet le plus fin est C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, Z). C'est lui qu'il conviendrait de considérer (au lieu de son "dual" ...) si on veut aborder b) c) d) sans conditions de finitude.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral homotopy-type models are an active topic (Mandell, Yuan's integral models, divided-power and derived-ring approaches). An explicit integral divided-power dg co-bialgebra of simplicial chains is an unexplored candidate model.

missed.claim: Construct the pd de Rham dg co-bialgebra with divided comultiplication, with duality and base change, and use it for Steenrod operations, minimal models and Künneth integrally. The construction is only asserted ('Il est possible de définir'), not carried out.
missed.quote: Il est possible de définir une cobigèbre diff. / C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, Z) (à comultipl. div.)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Spelling out this object and its homotopy theory would test whether pd de Rham forms give an integral analogue of Sullivan/Quillen theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction itself is a formal dualization (coend of duals of simplicial pd forms). The notable part is the methodological claim: in 1976, choose the integral divided-power coalgebra over the cochain algebra to avoid finiteness. This parallels Goerss's later coalgebraic approach and is unpublished, but it is a remark, not a worked result.
transcription_corrections: The coefficient ring transcribed as 'h' is almost certainly 'k' (the base ring, as on the previous page) throughout: C^·(X_*, k), Hom_k, ⊗_k k', 'k'-alg.', 'k-coaugmentation'.
In 'C_·(X_*, Z)' and 'C^{DRpd}_{··}(X_*, Z)', the Z appears written over an original 'k'.
In the last paragraph 'C^{**}_{DRpd}' should be 'C^{··}_{DRpd}' (double-dot bicomplex notation).
'(pas mieux filtrantes)' is better read as '(pas seulement filtrantes)', i.e. arbitrary colimits, not only filtered ones.
The formula line reads 'C_·(X_*, k) ≃ C_·(X_*, Z) ⊗_Z k'.
In the cochain formula the coefficient is k', i.e. 'C^·(X_*, k') ≃ Hom^·_Z(C_·(X_*, Z), k')'.
